Install

One command installs Whispy on macOS and Linux. Tick the steps as you go; your progress is remembered in this browser.

One-line installer

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/albrones/whispy/main/scripts/bootstrap.sh | bash

On macOS it installs Whispy V2, the native rewrite in Rust: it installs Rust and cmake if they are missing, builds and signs Whispy V2.app into /Applications, and launches it. An older Whispy.app (V1) is quit and moved to the Trash, since V2 replaces it. Source lives in ~/.local/share/whispy. Run the command again to update.

Under X11 the tray icon is optional: if your desktop has no working tray, Whispy runs without it (see troubleshooting).

On Linux it installs the system packages Whispy needs with apt, dnf or pacman (sudo asks for your password), then sets up a virtualenv and a systemd --user service. Source lives in ~/.local/share/whispy. Run the command again to update. Linux runs Whispy V1 (Python) until V2 reaches Linux, which is coming soon.

Checklist

  1. Run the one-line installer above. If the Xcode Command Line Tools are missing, it opens their installer: let it finish, then run the command again. The first build takes a few minutes. To do it by hand (with Rust and cmake installed): 
    git clone https://github.com/albrones/whispy.git
cd whispy && make v2-reinstall   # builds, signs, installs and launches Whispy V2.app
  2. Models. On first launch Whispy V2 downloads its speech models, about 1.2 GB (a notification says so). The menu says Ready when you can dictate.
  3. Microphone. At your first dictation macOS shows a Whispy V2 prompt: click Allow.
  4. Accessibility. System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility → enable Whispy V2. Without it the text is transcribed but never typed.
  5. Input Monitoring. System Settings → Privacy & Security → Input Monitoring → enable Whispy V2. It is needed to detect the Fn key.
  6. With Fn as the trigger, set System Settings → Keyboard → Press 🌐 key to → Do Nothing, or every tap also opens the emoji picker.
  7. Restart Whispy from its menu bar icon (Restart) so the new permissions apply.
  8. Switch on Start at login in the menu bar menu.

Whispy V2 is signed with a free, local self-signed certificate, so macOS remembers the permissions across updates. It keeps your settings from ~/.config/whispy/config.json and reuses the model V1 already downloaded, if any.

  1. Know your session. X11: Whispy listens to the trigger key itself. Wayland: your compositor's key binding calls the API (POST /start on press, POST /stop on release); there is no tray icon and errors arrive as notifications.
  2. Run the one-line installer above. It installs the missing system packages (the typing and clipboard tools for your session, PortAudio, and what pip needs to build), then a virtualenv and a systemd --user service that starts at login. Without apt, dnf or pacman, or to install them yourself (then set WHISPY_SKIP_SYSTEM_PACKAGES=1): 
    sudo apt install git python3-venv python3-dev gcc xdotool xclip libportaudio2   # Debian/Ubuntu, X11
sudo dnf install git python3-devel gcc xdotool xclip portaudio                  # Fedora, X11
sudo pacman -S git python gcc xdotool xclip portaudio                           # Arch, X11
sudo pacman -S git python gcc wtype wl-clipboard portaudio                      # Arch / Omarchy, Wayland
  3. Check that it is running: 
    systemctl --user status whispy.service
  4. On Omarchy (Hyprland): the installer links the omarchy-dictation-whispy backend into ~/.local/bin. It also links the Whispy bar widget into ~/.config/omarchy/plugins and puts its icon on the right of the bar. Select the backend once, then hold the dictation key (Right Alt by default; pick another in the Whispy panel). If Whispy is not running, the key shows « Whispy ne répond pas ». 
    omarchy-dictation-use whispy && hyprctl reload

Dictating mostly into a terminal under X11? Terminals read Ctrl+V as a literal character, so set copy_to_clipboard to false. Under Wayland the text is always typed with wtype (clipboard mode also leaves it on the clipboard), so terminals work as is.

First run: the model

Whispy uses one model, nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3, run on your CPU. It is downloaded once and cached: on Linux, about 639 MB the first time you dictate; on macOS, Whispy V2 downloads it at first launch with whisper small, which retries a dictation Parakeet heard nothing in (about 1.2 GB together, in ~/.whispy/models). It uses about 1.4 GB of memory while loaded.

It transcribes 25 languages and detects the language automatically: Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hungarian, Italian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Maltese, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Swedish, Russian and Ukrainian. Other languages will not transcribe.

Not working? Run make doctor from the source folder, or seeRead ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log, or see Troubleshooting.

Uninstall

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/albrones/whispy/main/scripts/bootstrap.sh | bash -s -- --uninstall

See Usage for the manual steps.
